gen_risks.description: Lingering political transition and economic uncertainty following the August 2024 government change could delay policy approvals, inter-ministerial coordination, and project execution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish early engagement with the Cabinet Division and key steering committees to maintain policy continuity, clear agency mandates, and timely adoption of guidelines.
gen_risks.evidence: An interim government was sworn in on August 8, 2024... lingering economic impact of the recent political transition.

gen_risks.description: High persistent inflation (9.9%) erodes the purchasing power and real benefit value of cash assistance provided to poor and vulnerable beneficiaries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and operationalize a standardized benefit adequacy framework to periodically review and index cash transfer benefit amounts against inflation metrics.
gen_risks.evidence: Inflation remained elevated, reaching 9.9 percent in January 2025... real value of benefits under the DSS's Old Age Allowance... has decreased.

gen_risks.description: High inclusion and exclusion errors (up to 60%) in existing safety nets risk excluding eligible poor households while directing resources to non-poor populations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Institutionalize a standardized Proxy Means Testing (PMT) module integrated into the Dynamic Social Registry (DSR) to dynamically score and target bottom-two-quintile households.
gen_risks.evidence: Nearly half (47 percent) of the poor households are not covered... inclusion and exclusion errors are approximately 60 percent.

gen_risks.description: Recurrent climate disasters such as floods and cyclones could disrupt project field operations, physical training sessions, and beneficiary access to local services.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize climate-vulnerable locations, house MIS platforms in disaster recovery centers, offer e-learning options, and disburse assistance electronically via G2P digital payments.
gen_risks.evidence: Recurring flooding affects more than 1 million people annually... A major flood in August 2024 affected over 3 million people.

gen_risks.description: Inter-ministerial coordination friction and delayed MoUs between the Finance Division, DSS, MoWCA, and other line ministries could stall the rollout of the Dynamic Social Registry.
gen_risks.mitigation: Form a high-level DSR Steering Committee chaired by the Cabinet Division and execute clear bilateral MoUs defining data-sharing and operational responsibilities across line ministries.
gen_risks.evidence: Past efforts to create a social registry... did not materialize due to... lack of institutional mandate to drive integration across ministries.

gen_risks.description: Vulnerabilities in interconnected digital MIS platforms could lead to data security breaches or misuse of personal citizen identification numbers (NID/BRN).
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce national data protection security standards, embed strict protocols into the Project Operations Manual, and host all software systems in secured National Data Centers.
gen_risks.evidence: GoB will adhere to its national data security regulations; the design of the DSR... will contain clear mitigation measures to address data security risks.

gen_risks.description: Financial management complexity across multiple implementing agencies, Designated Accounts, and sub-grant mechanisms could lead to accounting errors or disbursement bottlenecks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit certified FM consultants for each PIU, mandate the use of iBAS++ for integrated financial accounting, and implement regular internal and external audits.
gen_risks.evidence: From the FM perspective, the project design is complex due to the intricacy of activity selection and various IAs and finances.

gen_risks.description: Delays in establishing and fully staffing dedicated Project Implementation Units (PIUs) at DSS and SPBMU within legal covenant timelines could defer project launch.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mobilize experienced fiduciary and technical personnel from previous World Bank-financed project pools at DSS and closely track covenant compliance milestones.
gen_risks.evidence: The Recipient shall establish within six (6) months of the Effective Date... the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at the DSS.

gen_risks.description: Lower digital and financial literacy, combined with social norm constraints, may hinder poor women from accessing DSR registration and digital G2P cash payments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy user-friendly audio interfaces in local languages, engage frontline female social workers for outreach, and prioritize female-headed households for direct digital account setup.
gen_risks.evidence: Women report limited digital and financial access, which constrains their access to G2P payments... mobility constraints.

gen_risks.description: Failure or delay in achieving mandatory Performance-Based Conditions (PBCs) could halt results-based credit disbursements for eligible cash transfer program expenditures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide early technical assistance, conduct continuous internal monitoring of PBC indicators, and leverage floating PBC target timelines where allowed.
gen_risks.evidence: PBCs will be disbursed against the achievement of targets... Withdrawal applications must be supported by IUFRs confirming eligible expenditure.

gen_risks.description: Ad-hoc, low-quality, or market-disconnected skills training under livelihoods programs could fail to generate sustainable income or long-term poverty graduation for beneficiaries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update training curricula to combine technical skills with financial literacy, base courses on market assessments, and provide productive grants alongside mentorship.
gen_risks.evidence: training components are often ad hoc and limited in coverage and depth. Moreover, they do not currently provide training on financial literacy.

gen_risks.description: Financial mismanagement or inadequate oversight of sub-grant operating funds transferred directly to local social club bank accounts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate official social club enlistment with MoSW, require joint account signatories, perform registration due diligence, and enforce monthly SOE submissions approved by DSS officers.
gen_risks.evidence: Grants to social clubs under Subcomponent 2.2 will be financed through the DSS's DA and transferred directly by the DSS to the respective clubs' bank accounts.

gen_risks.description: Physical mobility barriers and lack of accessible infrastructure could exclude persons with disabilities (PWDs) and frail elderly from accessing project benefits and intake points.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish accessible local access points in every sub-district, deploy field social workers for home visits, and offer tailored cash-plus support and higher training stipends.
gen_risks.evidence: Mobility constraints also make it difficult for them to migrate during climate disasters... many shelters lack the necessary accessibility features.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk is Substantial. Safety and security concerns persist, despite the priority placed by the interim government on law and order. The interim government is implementing critical reforms before holding elections; reaching a consensus on reforms and the announcement of the election date could heighten political tensions among political parties and the interim government.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated during implementation through continuous engagement with all relevant government and nongovernmental entities, and dialogue with other stakeholders.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is Substantial. Downside risks have increased, related to uncertainties in the political process and the security situation which affects the recovery of economic activities. The financial sector remains vulnerable with deviations from international regulatory and supervisory standards and weak corporate governance. Despite recent improvements, the balance of payments remained in deficit and FX reserves remained under pressure.
gt_risks.mitigation: The macroeconomic risks are partially mitigated by the GoB's reform program, supported by International Monetary Fund arrangements, as well as ongoing World Bank and other development partners' policy lending. Data show consistent budgetary and political commitment to spending on safety nets across regimes in Bangladesh, with strong stakeholder consensus on ensuring a ring-fenced core budget for social assistance and livelihoods programs for the poorest.

gt_risks.description: The Fiduciary risk is rated Substantial due to the involvement of multiple implementing agencies (the DSS and FD), the complexity of activity selection, and intervention modalities. The project's residual procurement risk specifically is also rated Substantial, due to the complexity of procurement activities, multiagency coordination, and capacity limitations (para 56, part of the Fiduciary appraisal-summary discussion immediately preceding the Key Risks section).
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigation measures include hiring additional capacity, training, and close monitoring; considering satisfactory implementation of these measures, the residual fiduciary risk is assessed as Substantial and will be managed through proactive and continuous supervision and close dialogue with the GoB. Procurement-specific mitigation: hiring full-time procurement consultants for the DSS and FD; training on World Bank Procurement Regulations, STEP, and contract management; defining clear roles and streamlining approval processes; engaging IT procurement specialists and conducting early market assessments; using performance-based KPIs in contracts and including procurement consultants on bid evaluation committees; and establishing complaint registers at both agencies, with procurement not prior-reviewed by the Bank subject to regular fiduciary reviews and post-procurement review/audit by FAPAD.

gt_risks.description: The project presents a low environmental risk and a moderate social risk, resulting in an overall moderate environmental and social (ES) risk classification. Minor environmental concerns relate to potential e-waste generation from IT equipment and increased energy use. Social risks include potential exclusion of beneficiaries, inadequate consultation, and challenges in reaching remote and marginalized communities, including those who lack IT knowledge; there is also the likelihood of sexual exploitation and abuse/sexual harassment (SEA/SH) cases given the cash transfer modalities of the project and the interaction between service providers and beneficiaries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Waste management protocols and resource efficiency measures will prevent localized pollution. The project will establish a Digital Social Registry (DSR) to improve targeting and coverage, complemented by a robust outreach and monitoring program, and will include Stakeholder Engagement Plan provisions requiring community consultation and disclosure measures. The existing DSS grievance redress mechanism (GRM) will address complaints. An SEA/SH Action Plan will be developed including code of conduct, awareness raising, and GRM to address potential incidents. The project will partially rely on the borrower's ES management framework supplemented by gap-filling measures included in the POM.
